provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1862 carries `sequentem Oratio` here, which the CMAA text layer of the 1962 does not; the 1862 lacks `JLJ`, which the 1962 prints; the 1862 reads `fllecebras` where the 1962 reads `illecebras` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `intercessi6nefid6 les` where the 1962 reads `intercessione fideles`; the 1862 reads `terr6na` where the 1962 reads `terrena` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1862 reads `ccel6stia` where the 1962 reads `cselestia` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); 5 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1862 prints no conclusion at this place; the 1962 prints `Per Dominum`; the 1862 sets 8 point(s) of punctuation in this oration where the 1962 sets 5; the 1922 Mame reads `sequentem Oratio EUS` where the 1962 reads `Deus`; the 1922 Mame lacks `JLJ`, which the 1962 prints; the 1922 Mame reads `virtute constantiz` where the 1962 reads `virtiite constantiae` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1922 Mame reads `quéesumus` where the 1962 reads `qusesumus` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); the 1922 Mame reads `celéstia` where the 1962 reads `cselestia` (letterforms inferred, not read: the difference is at the level of the recogniser); 3 further place(s) differ only in orthography, ligature or the recogniser's letterforms; the 1922 Mame prints no conclusion at this place; the 1962 prints `Per Dominum`. Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 541 (artifact PDF p. 655), target-body character coverage 0.95, found by a sweep; Benziger 1962 conformed printing, target-body character coverage 0.90. Recorded limitation: The 1962 prints this under 03-04 with the rubric Missa Os justi, de Communi Confessoris non Pontificis I loco [24], praeter orationem sequentem. Every 1862 reading here rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone; this lane has no page image of the 1862, and the recogniser damages roughly one word in three there, so where the 1862's letterforms differ from the 1962's the difference recorded above is an inference from the layer and not a reading of the leaf. The 1922 Mame is the check on those places, and it is a full public-domain peer rather than mere corroboration. Not checked: the 1962 page image for this oration, the 1570 (its recogniser is too degraded to control a claim), and the 1604 except where named. || REPAIRED by lane repair-2 on 2026-09-03. The stored target had been a text-layer reading carrying recogniser damage; it has been replaced word for word by a reading taken from the 1962 CMAA facsimile page image at 400 dpi (artifact PDF p. 564, printed folio read on the same image). Line-end hyphens are joined, printed stress accents are dropped, and the ae/oe ligatures are expanded to two letters; punctuation, capitalisation and the conclusion are reproduced at the length the page prints them. The verdict, the antecedent locus and the recorded differences are the original lane's and were not revisited. The marginal number 2238 already in the locus was confirmed on the same 400 dpi image; the printed folio 483 stands in the running head of the same crop.
